summary: Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts, Leiden, and ANU under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later directing the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Akitoshi Saito worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as professor and later professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 1982, 2014) and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Akong Tulku Rinpoche was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He co-founded Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre in 1967 and served as its abbot (attested 2009).
Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She is a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago and a researcher at Ghent University (both attested 2026).
Akshay Ramanlal Desai was a historian and sociologist. He studied at the University of Mumbai from approximately 1940 to 1946 under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye.

Alan Avdagić works in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held a post at the University of Würzburg and studied as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Free University of Berlin (attested 2026).
Alan Butterworth was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at Elizabeth College and Balliol College, Oxford (c. 1883–1885), and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1885 to 1918.
Alan Entwistle specialized in Indology and religious studies. He completed his studies at the University of Southampton (c. 1968–1971) and SOAS University of London (c. 1971–1982).

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD from Temple University, he taught at the University of Delaware as professor (1992) and associate professor of philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

Alan Gerard Wagner specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, having also studied with Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans was an art and architectural historian. He completed his studies at the University of Toronto (1946) and Princeton University (1948, 1950).

Alan John Bayard Wace was an archaeologist who studied at Pembroke College, Cambridge under Robert Alexander Neil. He held posts at the British School at Athens, the Victoria and Albert Museum, the University of Cambridge, and Alexandria University.

Alan Lomax was an ethnomusicologist. He attended Choate Rosemary Hall, St. Mark's School of Texas, Harvard University (c. 1933–1934), the University of Texas at Austin (c. 1934–1936), and Columbia University (c. 1939–1940).
Alan Nussbaum is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University from approximately 1969 to 1976 and served as a faculty member at Cornell University from around 1985 to 2021.

Alan Sponberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and taught at Stanford University (attested 1988).

Alan Watts was a philosopher of religion. He studied at Bexley Seabury Seminary, held an Episcopal chaplaincy at Northwestern University (1944–1950), and taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies and the Esalen Institute.

Alasdair MacIntyre was a philosopher who studied at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Manchester. His academic posts included positions at the University of Essex, Brandeis University, Duke University, and the University of Notre Dame.

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who completed degrees at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Pittsburgh. He held posts at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and the University of Toronto (emeritus professor 1986).

Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. After completing his PhD at the University of Cambridge, he held posts at the Singapore University of Technology and Design, SOAS, and the Pali Text Society.
Albert Debrunner was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Jacob Wackernagel and Ferdinand Sommer. He held professorships at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Bern, Jena, and Basel.
